name: gdc-hcmi-cmdc
alternateName: NCI Cancer Model Development for the Human Cancer Model Initiative
description:
The Human Cancer Models Initiative exists to replace ageing immortalised cell lines with models that retain patient genomics and come with their source tumor characterized. Coverage is exceptionally uniform: whole genome on 804 of 805, RNA sequencing on 781, exome on 721, methylation on 703, and both histopathology and radiology on 382.
Its distinctive value is breadth across tumor types, including rare cancers that have no established model system at all. Prior treatment is recorded for 92% of donors, which matters because it determines what the derived model actually represents.
citeAs: NCI Cancer Model Development for the Human Cancer Model Initiative

supportedQuestions: How faithfully do patient-derived models retain the genomics of their source tumor?
Can a usable model system be found for a rare cancer that currently has none?
Does prior treatment of the donor shape the derived model's biology?
inappropriateUses: Treating model results as clinical evidence.
